children: President Donald Trump rejected concerns over his plan to pay $5,000 dividend checks to Americans, affirming that "we can easily handle that because we're taking in so much money."
"The $5,000 is going to happen 100%," Trump said on Sunday. "And the reason is because our country is taking in trillions and trillions of dollars."
Trump last week proposed sending $5,000 checks to every American adult if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate in the midterms.
On Sunday, he told reporters he didn't want to send the checks now "because if the Democrats get in, our country will be in shambles, and they won't be able to do it."
While Trump said he didn't think Congress needed to approve the dividend payout, House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA) said "he'd need Congress to act."
if he'd commit to carrying out Trump's dividend plan, Johnson said he'd "commit that Congress will work through it and find consensus on that."

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick previously said the dividend checks would not come from taxpayer money and the administration could "earn the money" that Trump wants to pay out, without specifying how.
Sending the $5,000 checks would cost around $1.2T. The U.S. government is already projected to run a budget deficit of nearly $1.9T in FY 2027.

"Spending upwards of $1T on a new one-time payment program would balloon the deficit to nearly $3T, even with the new revenue coming in from the president's tariffs," Erica York, senior economist at the Tax Foundation, estimated. "It would take almost a decade of collections from tariffs to cover the cost."
